cards.title: 1% left
cards.body:
Your phone hits **1%** just as you need it most. Or you plug it in overnight and wake up to a flat battery.

Power problems are some of the most common device problems, and many of them are easy to fix, or to avoid altogether.

cards.title: Inside the battery
cards.body:
Phones and laptops use **lithium-ion batteries**. They store a lot of energy in a small, light pack. The amount they hold is measured in **watt-hours (Wh)**: a phone battery holds about 15 Wh, and a laptop's a few times more.

Everything the device does uses some energy, but the biggest drains are usually the **screen's brightness**, **location (GPS)** and **apps busy in the background**.

Batteries also wear out slowly. After a few hundred full charges they hold noticeably less, and **heat** wears them out faster, so keep devices out of hot cars and don't charge them under a pillow. If one gets too hot, stop, unplug it and let it cool on a table out of the sun (never in the fridge or freezer).

An old battery can also **swell**: the case bulges or the screen lifts. Stop using it, don't press it, and tell an adult.

cards.title: When it won't charge
cards.body:
Cables and chargers wear out far more often than phones, so first try **another cable and another socket**.

Pocket fluff can also pack into the **charging port**. With the phone switched off, an adult can help brush it out gently with a soft, dry brush. **Never use metal** (like a pin or paper clip) **or water**. If that doesn't work, a repair shop can clean it safely.

cards.prompt: You plug your phone in before bed, but the charging symbol doesn't appear.

steps.text: What's the simplest thing to try first?

choices.text: Try a different cable and a different plug socket
choices.consequence: Good: cables and chargers wear out far more often than phones do.

choices.text: Poke a pin into the charging port
choices.consequence: Never put metal in the port. It can scratch the contacts or cause a short circuit.

steps.text: The other cable charges a friend's phone, but still not yours. With a torch you can see the port is **packed with pocket fluff**.

choices.text: Phone off, ask an adult to help brush it out with a soft, dry brush
choices.consequence: Out comes the fluff, and the cable clicks in properly. It's charging! If it hadn't worked, a repair shop could clean it safely.

choices.text: Dig it out with a paper clip
choices.consequence: Metal can damage the port or short it out. Use something soft, or let a repair shop do it.
Water and electronics don't mix. It could damage the phone for good.

cards.explanation: Start with the simplest fix: **another cable and socket**. Fluff in the port is common: with the phone off, an adult can gently brush it out with something soft and dry. **Never metal, never water.** If in doubt, a repair shop can do it.

cards.prompt: Tap the **charging port**, where the fluff was hiding.
cards.explanation: The **charging port** is on the bottom edge. It's open to the outside, which is why pocket fluff collects in it.

cards.prompt: You've got a long coach trip. Make the battery last **at least 8 hours**, and keep your **music** playing.
cards.explanation: The screen at full brightness was the biggest drain. Turning it down, switching off location and stopping background apps (or using **low power mode**) all stretch the battery. Music on its own uses very little.

cards.prompt: Does each habit **help** the battery, or **drain or damage** it?

items.label: Low power mode on a long day
Keeping it out of the hot sun
Leaving it in a hot car
Location on for every app, all day

cards.explanation: Lower brightness and low power mode save charge. **Heat** is a battery's enemy: hot cars and charging under a pillow (which traps heat) wear it out faster. Location on all day keeps draining it.

cards.prompt: An old laptop's case is **bulging**, and the trackpad is being pushed up from underneath. What should you do?

options.text: Stop using it, unplug it, and tell an adult
Keep using it, as long as it still turns on

cards.explanation: A bulge often means the **battery is swelling**. A swollen lithium battery can catch fire if it's pressed, bent or punctured. Stop using it, unplug it, keep it away from anything that can burn, and **tell an adult**. A repair shop can replace the battery safely.

cards.prompt: You're gaming on your bed with the phone plugged in.

steps.text: The phone is really hot, and a message says **"Phone needs to cool down."**

choices.text: Put it in the freezer to cool it quickly
choices.consequence: Sudden cold can make water droplets form inside the phone. Let it cool down slowly.
The phone will slow down to protect itself, and all that heat wears out the battery.

choices.text: Stop, unplug it and leave it on a table out of the sun
choices.consequence: It cools down safely in a few minutes.

steps.text: A week later, the back of the phone looks **puffed up** and the screen is lifting at one edge.

choices.text: Stop using it and tell an adult so it can go to a repair shop
choices.consequence: A puffed-up phone often has a swollen battery. A repair shop can replace it safely.
Pressing on a swollen battery can make it catch fire. Leave it alone and tell an adult.

cards.explanation: An overheating phone needs to **stop, unplug and cool down slowly** on a hard surface out of the sun. Never freeze it. A phone that looks puffed up may have a **swollen battery**: stop using it, don't press it, and tell an adult.

cards.prompt: Label the parts of the phone that power flows through, plus two that use lots of it.
cards.explanation: Power comes in through the **charging port**, is stored in the **battery**, and reaches the board through the **battery connector**. The **CPU** and **camera** are two of the hungriest parts, along with the screen.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **Brightness, location and background apps** drain the battery most. Low power mode helps.
- **Heat** wears batteries out. Keep devices out of the sun and don't charge them under pillows.
- Won't charge? Try **another cable and socket** first. For fluff, an adult can gently brush the port with something soft and dry: never metal or water.
- A **bulging** device may have a swollen battery. Stop using it, don't press it, and tell an adult.

One quiz left: the course final.
